Owner found the actual root cause after this session's multi-hour, multi-revert debugging saga: an INNER_SHADOW (or any) effect on a frame with NO FILL corrupts Figma's own text rendering for that frame's descendants -- specifically observed with Plus Jakarta Sans as a variable font (fontName.variationSettings, a weight-axis instance). This was Row's own divider implementation the whole time -- an INNER_SHADOW 'flood a 1px line at the bottom' effect on Row's own frame, which has no fill by design (rows in a recessed scroll track stay transparent). Every one of this session's three prior theories (text-style redefinition, instance-level text overrides, 'any sustained document activity') were each individually disproven by isolated testing -- all were red herrings; the real constant across every corrupted repro was simply 'an effect exists on this no-fill frame', which held in literal every attempt including the ones with zero text-style or instance touches, because the corrupting effect lived on the MASTER, inherited by every instance regardless of what else was or wasn't touched in a given attempt.
Fixed by replacing the effect with a real per-side stroke: strokeBottomWeight=1, strokeTopWeight/strokeLeftWeight/strokeRightWeight=0, strokeAlign='INSIDE', strokesIncludedInLayout=false (Card's own established inset-stroke technique, reused). Applied to the 12 non-focus variants (default+hover); the 6 focus variants keep their existing all-sides ring untouched, since it already visually covers the bottom edge with a more prominent color -- no conflict, no need for a second stroke layer. Verified via read-back: all 18 variants confirmed zero effects, correct stroke weights, focus ring intact where expected. Verified via export: text renders perfectly, zero corruption, across the full ListCard with all 9 live fleet rows (confirmed inherited the fix automatically, zero per-instance changes needed).
This attempt also redid the slot rename (plain 'status'/'action', no '(convert to Slot)' suffix) in the same pass -- both fixes landed clean together with no interaction (renaming layers has nothing to do with effects/fills, confirmed by this being the Nth time renaming alone was tested in isolation without ever corrupting anything).

General lesson for this file going forward, not just Row: never put an effect (shadow of any kind) directly on a frame that has no fill. New, expensive-to-find gotcha: figma.Node.insertChild/appendChild fails with 'Cannot move node. New parent is an instance or is inside of an instance' when the target Slot is nested 2+ instance-levels deep (e.g. Modal instance -> column frame -> ScrollableArea INSTANCE's own content Slot) -- regardless of whether the outer context is a component's master or an already-placed canvas instance. It does NOT matter whether you're editing a master vs a live instance; what matters is how many instance boundaries the target slot sits behind. A Slot belonging to a single, non-nested instance (e.g. a bare cloned frame's own direct ScrollableArea instance) accepts insertChild fine -- confirmed both from the EntityProblemPanel build (worked, 1 instance level) and from two independent failures trying to add Row instances into RigProblemDetail's per-column ScrollableArea slot (failed both on the master and on a placed instance, 2 instance levels: Modal > ScrollableArea).
Workaround used: scrollArea.detachInstance() on the specific ScrollableArea instance that needs new rows -- detaching converts it (and its Slot) to plain frames with no instance boundary, after which clone/insertChild/appendChild all work normally. Renamed the detached frame and its content frame back to ScrollableArea/content for clarity. This sacrifices that one column's live link to the ScrollableArea component (its border/background/overflow styling stays, but it will not pick up future ScrollableArea master changes) -- acceptable for a content-specific screen instance, not something to do on a component master meant for reuse.
Also separately: for Row's `description` when it's a LabelGroup instance (not plain text) and only a single description line is needed, don't try to delete+replace the LabelGroup node (same instance-insertion restriction, plus it's a full node removal) -- instead retext the LabelGroup's first Label child and set the other Label(s) + divider(s) to visible=false. Property overrides (text content, visibility, component swap) work at any nesting depth; only NEW node creation is restricted.

Built Slider (React), a single-thumb range control, size sm/md/lg reusing ProgressBar's exact track scale (8/12/16px) on the reasoning that a slider is a progress bar you can drag. Built on a real native <input type="range"> for free keyboard/drag/ARIA support, controlled-or-uncontrolled via the same seed-internal-state-from-defaultValue pattern, mandatory aria-label/aria-labelledby union type matching ProgressBar/IconButton. Went through 2 real implementation bugs before landing correctly. Bug 1 (real, confirmed): a CSS rule comma-combining a ::-webkit-* selector with a ::-moz-* one (e.g. `.x[data-size=sm]::-webkit-slider-thumb, .x[data-size=sm]::-moz-range-thumb { width: 16px; height: 16px; }`) gets silently dropped IN ITS ENTIRETY by Chrome, because an unrecognized vendor pseudo-element invalidates the whole selector list for a plain style rule (not a forgiving list like :is()/:where()) -- confirmed by dumping document.styleSheets via javascript_tool and seeing the per-size track/thumb dimension rules simply absent from the parsed CSSOM while the base (non-comma) rules were present. Fixed by splitting every such pair into two separate single-selector rules everywhere in the file. Bug 2 turned out to be a FALSE ALARM, not a real bug: after fixing bug 1, one demo slider (value=0, i.e. percent=0%) appeared to render with no visible track at all, reproducing across full page reloads and even a full dev-server restart, which looked exactly like a genuine Chromium rendering quirk (hypothesized: ::-webkit-slider-runnable-track background fails to paint when value===min). Spent real effort chasing this -- rewrote the whole component to a more robust architecture (real input made fully transparent except its thumb, with a separate plain decorative track+fill span pair underneath, mirroring ProgressBar's own track/fill DOM shape instead of a vendor-gradient hack) specifically to sidestep the suspected bug. The rewrite still showed the exact same 'invisible track at 0%' symptom even though it no longer used any pseudo-element background or gradient at all -- which finally proved the real cause: the throwaway vite harness's own index.html had `body { background: #f4f4f5 }`, and color.surface.sunken (the track's own background token) resolves to EXACTLY #f4f4f5 (zinc.100) -- at 0% fill the entire track is that flat sunken color, which is visually indistinguishable from the page background behind it. Confirmed conclusively by setting document.body.style.background to white via javascript_exec and seeing every track (including the 0% one) render correctly. This was never a component bug, Chromium bug, or even related to value=0 specifically -- purely a coincidental color match in a disposable test page. Kept the rewritten track/fill-as-plain-divs architecture anyway despite the false-alarm origin, since it's a genuine improvement on its own merits (consistent with ProgressBar's own pattern, no reliance on vendor-prefixed pseudo-element styling beyond the thumb, which needs it regardless) -- but corrected the component's own doc comments to NOT claim the false 'Chromium value===min bug', describing the real (true) rationale instead (avoiding fragile vendor-prefixed background styling in general, consistency with ProgressBar). Also found and fixed one more small real bug during the same debugging pass: the .fill span was plain `display: inline` (a <span>'s default), so its `width`/`height` CSS silently had zero effect (per spec, width/height don't apply to inline non-replaced elements) -- fixed with `display: block`. Also suppressed the native input's own default focus outline (which was drawing an ugly orange rectangle around the whole invisible input box) in favor of the custom :focus-visible box-shadow ring already applied to the thumb. Verified keyboard interaction via the Browser pane's `key` action -- first attempt used the key name 'Right', which the browser did not recognize as the actual ArrowRight key (keydown listeners fired but no native stepping occurred); switching to the correct DOM key name 'ArrowRight' worked immediately and updated the controlled value end to end. npm run typecheck and npm run build both clean.

Ported all 5 table-related components built in Figma earlier today into React: Pagination, TableHeaderCell, TableCell (+ TableCellText, TableProgressStages), TableRow, Table. Deliberately used real semantic HTML instead of a div/flex re-implementation of the Figma structure -- Table renders a real <table>, TableRow a real <tr>, TableHeaderCell/TableCell real <th>/<td>. This wasn't just an aesthetic choice: it directly answers a question from earlier in this same conversation ('if cell width is hug, how will it align with cells in rows below') that had no good answer in Figma (the old table's own fragility -- manually keeping every cell's width in sync per column by hand -- was literally what prompted the redesign) -- a real HTML table's layout engine solves this automatically, every cell in a column gets the same width with zero manual coordination. Made several deliberate simplifications relative to the literal Figma variant structure, in each case because a real interactive DOM element can do something a static Figma reference fundamentally can't: (1) TableRow has no variant prop at all -- header-vs-body is purely 'does this row happen to sit inside a <thead> or a <tbody>', which Table controls by literally wrapping the header prop in <thead> and children in <tbody>, and TableRow's own CSS keys off that ancestor context via plain 'thead .row'/'tbody .row' descendant selectors (untouched by CSS Modules scoping since thead/tbody aren't classes) rather than needing a prop to be told. (2) TableRow has no hover/active props either -- a real <tr> gets :hover and :focus-within for free, so only 'status: danger|success' (a genuine fact about the row's data, not an interaction state) needed an explicit prop; hover is implemented as the same inset box-shadow wash technique the original Row/ScrollableArea hover already uses (color.table.row.shadow.hover, an alpha-black-3% token, layered via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1000px rather than a background swap), and active/focus is a :focus-within outline (1px, color.table.row.border.active -> color.border.focus, outline-offset -1px to draw inward) with NO background change, matching the owner's own final decision on that from earlier in this session. (3) TableCell's 9 Figma content variants collapsed to a single plain, fully transparent <td> (no fill -- TableRow owns all visible row color, confirmed against the exact bug this had in Figma before the fill was removed there) plus exactly 2 new small components: TableCellText (icon+title+supporting-text, with an emphasis:'default'|'strong' prop merging what Figma had to keep as two separate variants -- text/textStrong -- purely because Figma variants can't parameterize a color the way a real prop can; colors matched to the OWNER's actual final Figma tuning, not my own original proposal: default emphasis uses color.text.strong, strong emphasis uses color.text.default (the darkest step), supporting text follows muted->subtle) and TableProgressStages (the dot/line stage tracker, mandatory aria-label same union-type pattern as ProgressBar, role=progressbar with real aria-valuenow/min/max) -- badge/action/iconOnly needed zero new code, already fully composable by dropping a real Badge/Button/IconButton directly into a plain TableCell. Owner spotted a visible corner/kink artifact in the diagonal stripe lines right at the pill's rounded end-caps. Fixed by extending every line's length by one full tile-height beyond each original endpoint (same slope/position along the diagonal, just longer) so the tips always fall well outside whatever the rounded-cap boundary clips away, regardless of corner radius - the visible clipped portion is unchanged, only the invisible overshoot differs. This bug and fix is Figma-only (the vector-line technique standing in for a native repeating pattern) - React's CSS repeating-linear-gradient has no equivalent failure mode since it tiles as a true infinite background, not discrete line segments with endpoints.
